# Metering demo — a supplier half-hourly file, read and explained

```bash
iaiops meter check demo/metering/college_hh_sample.csv
iaiops meter profile demo/metering/college_hh_sample.csv \
    --tariff demo/metering/tariff_example.yaml \
    --site "Example FE College (synthetic)" --report college.html
```

No hardware, no network: the input is a file.

## ⚠️ Read this before showing it to anyone

**Everything here is synthetic.** `college_hh_sample.csv` is generated by
`generate_sample.py` (fixed seed) and is shaped like a small further-education
college; the MPAN is not a real supply number. `tariff_example.yaml` is an
**illustrative** three-rate tariff — its prices and its "red" band times are
placeholders, not any supplier's or DNO's figures. Quote the *mechanism*, never
the pounds.

## What the file contains on purpose

| | where | what the report should do |
|---|---|---|
| heating/ventilation running to 21:00 Mon–Thu | every term-time week | show it in the heatmap and in the out-of-hours figures |
| a lighter half-term week | 26–30 Oct 2026 | lower weekday bars in the daily chart |
| the autumn clock change | 25 Oct 2026 (50 half hours) | read all 50 — the file has 50 period columns |
| a data-collector gap | 3 Nov 2026 10:00–16:00 | count 12 missing half hours, draw the day amber, **not** scale the total up |
| estimated reads | 14–16 Sep 2026 (`Read Type = E`) | report the estimated share of kWh |

Regenerate with:

```bash
python demo/metering/generate_sample.py > demo/metering/college_hh_sample.csv
```
